PLACES IN THE COMMUNITY LESSON · PLACES IN THE COMMUNITY · AGES 3–5 YEARS

Sports Center — a step-by-step lesson for grown-up and child

This lesson teaches what a sports center is and how to try a new game there — rain or shine.

What is this?

A sports center is a big building full of ways to move: a swimming pool, courts for ball games, a gym, and a timetable of classes for every age.

What does it mean?

A roof over play is the idea: rain cannot cancel games that live indoors — the sports center keeps the town moving all winter.

What does the child need to know?

You need sport shoes, a water bottle, and the one thing nobody can lend you: the willingness to try something new in front of strangers who are all trying too.

Why this matters

Not every family has a garden big enough for games — the center shares one with the whole town, plus a pool that steams in January.

What it teaches

Trying new movements (splash, bounce, balance), following a class leader, water confidence, and the social skill of joining a game already in progress.

Words to learn

sports centerleisure centrepoolcourtgymclasstimetableteamtryshoes

Say this to your child

“"The sports center! Look at the board — swimming today! Shoes on, bottle filled, towel over the shoulder. Into the shallow end — splash! Kick those legs! And when class is done we say the magic words: AGAIN tomorrow!"”

Step by step

  1. Read the timetable together — the wall board lists everything: swim times, ball times, tiny-gym times.
  2. Pack the kit: shoes, bottle, towel, and the lucky sock if there is one (there is always one).
  3. Try the thing: the pool (splash in the shallow end first — everyone does), the court, the soft floor.
  4. Copy the leader — arms up, arms down — nobody is watching anyone else; they are all busy wobbling too.
  5. Finish with water and the two words: "AGAIN tomorrow." The timetable says yes.

Look closer at the picture

On the card, the round window rolls in like a soccer ball over the sports center doors — the building plays too, and it is telling you so.

Ask your child

"What lives at the sports center?" (a pool, courts, classes — every game under one roof) "What do we bring?" (shoes, a water bottle, a towel) "What are the magic words at the end?" (AGAIN tomorrow!)

What your child can say or do

Your child might run family mini-olympics with paper medals and a mandatory anthem, copy the class leader so faithfully the leader notices, or post the timetable results on the fridge like league tables.

Out in the real world

American families say sports center; British families say leisure centre — same courts, same chlorine smell. Most centers run cheap kids’ swim and soft-play sessions; the timetable is a whole winter’s worth of Tuesdays.

Try it together

Family mini-olympics on any flat floor: sock-ball toss into laundry baskets, hallway bowling, a balance-beam line of tape, medal ceremony at the end — paper medals, national anthem optional, absolutely sung.

Understanding check

Ask: "Why do games keep going when it rains?" (they live indoors — under the roof) "What do we say after class?" (AGAIN tomorrow!)

This lesson pairs with the Sports Center flashcard in the library — print it, show it, keep it on the fridge. Back to Places in the Community.
